function: Over-the-air aggregation of local gradients via RIS-assisted AirComp, with RIS-assisted SWIPT model broadcast; joint device selection, beamforming, power splitting and RIS coefficients (p. 2-3).
system: AP with M=10 antennas, passive reflecting RIS with N=40 elements, U=10 single-antenna devices; Rician fading; no frequency band stated (p. 3, 11).
method: Federated training of a linear regression model and a fully connected MNIST network; RIS and beamformers designed by alternating optimization and SCA, not learned (p. 3, 13).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss with Rician fading (factors 0, 0, infinity), synthetic linear-regression data and MNIST for the learning task; no standard channel model or measurements (p. 11-13).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing; sweeps of number of devices and SNR requirement; MNIST accuracy on 10,000 test samples; no new scenario (p. 12-14).
baselines: Error-Free ideal aggregation, Random RIS Coefficients, Without RIS; no earlier learned method or published aggregation design compared (p. 11).
metrics: Harvested power, convergence of algorithms (objective versus iterations), FL training loss for linear regression, MNIST test accuracy (p. 12-14).
complexity: Order of complexity of the DL-SWIPT and UL-AirComp algorithms in U, M, N (exponent 3.5) and iteration counts; SCA iterations plotted (p. 10-12).
q1_support: p. 11: "we consider the Rician fading to model the small-scale fading"; custom path-loss plus Rician simulator, with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "the test accuracy results are obtained based on the 10 000 test samples"; a held-out part of MNIST, and no new scenario, band or configuration is used for testing (the number of devices varies only for the optimizer convergence, p. 12).
q3_support: p. 11: "Error-Free", "Random RIS Coefficients" and "Without RIS" are the benchmarks, all defined by the paper itself; no earlier published aggregation design or learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall complexity of Algorithm 2 is given by" a big-O expression in U, M and N; p. 11: "the overall complexity of Algorithm 3 is" also given as big-O.
q5_support: p. 13: "an image identification task based on the MNIST data set"; this is a learning-task dataset only, the channel is simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Over-the-air FL (RIS plus SWIPT): the learned element is the FL model trained across devices (linear regression, MNIST), so it passes the no_learning check; the transceiver and RIS design is optimization (AO, SCA), not learned. Area 7 (over-the-air aggregation). Table I of p. 11 was read from the page image.
